Lemma
[length expansion under a metric-expanding map]

↗ def:dc-ch7-2-4 ↗ def:dc-ch1-2-9

1. ch7:3.3Let $f:M\to N$ be a differentiable map between Riemannian manifolds which expands the metric: $|df_p(v)|\ge |v|$ for every $p\in M$ and every $v\in T_pM$. Then for every piecewise differentiable curve $\bar c:[a,b]\to M$, \[ \ell (f\circ \bar c)\ \ge \ \ell (\bar c)\ \ge \ d\big(\bar c(a),\bar c(b)\big). \] In particular $d\big(\bar c(a),\bar c(b)\big)\le \ell (f\circ \bar c)$: the source distance between the endpoints of a curve is bounded by the length of its image.
Proof

↗ def:dc-ch7-2-4 \sketch Along a piecewise differentiable curve, $|d(f\circ \bar c)/dt|\ge |d\bar c/dt|$. Integrating yields $\ell (f\circ \bar c)\ge \ell (\bar c)$, and the definition of distance gives the second inequality.

□
